senses.definition: The watery liquid your mouth makes to moisten food and start breaking it down.
senses.example: Saliva helps make a dry cracker easier to swallow.

senses.definition: An open area of grass with scattered trees, often in a warm place with a wet season and a dry season.
senses.example: Zebras grazed on the savanna while birds rested in a tree.

senses.definition: To speak words or show a message in writing.
senses.example: Mari said we should wait until the light turned green.

senses.definition: A chance to give your opinion or help make a decision.
senses.example: Each team member had a say in choosing the name.

senses.definition: A tool that shows how heavy something is.
senses.example: I put the apples on the kitchen scale.

senses.definition: The way a distance in a map or a size in a model compares to the real distance or size.
senses.example: The map’s scale shows that one inch on the page stands for ten miles.

senses.definition: One of the small, thin pieces on the outside of many fish and reptiles.
senses.example: Each scale on the fish caught a bit of light.

senses.definition: A set of musical notes played in order from low to high or high to low.
senses.example: I practiced a scale on the piano before playing my song.

senses.definition: To climb up or over something tall or difficult.
senses.example: The climbers wore safety gear to scale the wall.

senses.definition: The salt water that covers much of Earth, or one particular part of that water.
senses.example: From the hill we could see the sea and the boats far away.

senses.definition: To notice something with your eyes.
senses.example: We saw three birds sitting on a wire.

senses.definition: To understand what someone means or how something works.
senses.example: I see why both pieces need to be the same length now.

senses.definition: A plant part that holds a tiny young plant and can grow into a new plant in the right conditions.
senses.example: We planted a bean seed in a cup of soil.

senses.definition: To put seeds in or on the ground so plants can grow.
senses.example: We will seed the bare patch of lawn in spring.

senses.definition: A place or collection that stores seeds to preserve different plants for the future.
senses.example: The seed bank stored seeds from many kinds of rice.

senses.definition: The store of seeds already in the soil in a place.
senses.example: After rain, some seeds in the soil’s seed bank began to grow.

senses.definition: To cause a thing, message, or person to go to another place.
senses.example: We sent a postcard to our cousins.

senses.definition: An animal related to a goat, often raised for its wool, milk, or meat.
senses.example: The farmer counted six sheep in the field.

senses.definition: To give off light or look bright as light bounces off something.
senses.example: The full moon shone above the rooftops.

senses.definition: To make something look bright by cleaning or polishing it.
senses.example: I shined my shoes for the concert.

senses.definition: To let someone see something, or help them see how to do it.
senses.example: I showed my friend how to fold a paper boat.

senses.definition: A performance or program for people to see or hear.
senses.example: The school put on a puppet show.

senses.definition: A sign or message that tells what is happening or what to do.
senses.example: The bell was our signal to go inside.

senses.definition: To send someone a sign or message.
senses.example: We waved to signal that we were ready.

senses.definition: To make music with your voice by moving among notes.
senses.example: We sang a song on the bus.

senses.definition: To rest your body on your bottom with the upper part of your body usually upright.
senses.example: We sat on a bench to rest our feet.

senses.definition: A muscle that can help move your body by pulling on a bone.
senses.example: A skeletal muscle in your upper arm helps bend your elbow.

senses.definition: To be in the natural resting state in which you are less aware of things around you and may dream.
senses.example: I slept until the birds started to sing.

senses.definition: The natural period of rest when a person or animal is asleep.
senses.example: A night of good sleep helped me feel ready for school.

senses.definition: The Sun and the objects held near it by gravity, including planets, moons, comets, and asteroids. Systems around other stars are often called planetary systems.
senses.example: Earth is one of eight planets in our solar system.

senses.definition: A kind of matter that keeps its own shape under ordinary conditions.
senses.example: Ice is a solid, but it can melt into liquid water.

senses.definition: Made of material all the way through, with no empty middle.
senses.example: The toy was carved from one solid piece of wood.

senses.definition: Firm or strong enough to stay steady.
senses.example: The table needed a solid base so it would not wobble.

senses.definition: Vibrations that travel through material such as air, water, or a wall and can often be heard.
senses.example: The sound of the bell reached us from across the playground.

senses.definition: To make a noise or to seem a certain way to someone who hears you.
senses.example: You sound excited about your trip.

senses.definition: In good condition or based on good reasons.
senses.example: The builder checked that the old steps were sound.

senses.definition: To use your voice to say words. It can also mean being able to use a language.
senses.example: She spoke slowly so the whole class could follow.

senses.definition: A group of living things of the same kind. Members of many species can have young with one another, though scientists also use other clues to tell species apart.
senses.example: The blue whale and the humpback whale are different species.

senses.definition: A thick bundle of nerve tissue protected by the backbone that carries many messages between the brain and body.
senses.example: Signals that help move your foot can travel through your spinal cord.

senses.definition: To stay upright on your feet.
senses.example: We stood at the fence to watch the parade.

senses.definition: A frame or base that holds an object up.
senses.example: The music stand held the pages at the right height.

senses.definition: A small place where people sell or hand out things.
senses.example: A roadside stand sold baskets of berries.

senses.definition: A huge ball of hot gas in space that gives off its own light. The Sun is the nearest one to Earth.
senses.example: A star can look like a tiny point because it is so far away.

senses.definition: A shape with points sticking out from the center.
senses.example: We drew a five-pointed star on the card.

senses.definition: A person who is especially well known for performing or doing something.
senses.example: She became a basketball star.

senses.definition: To play one of the main parts in a show, film, or play.
senses.example: I hope to star in the school play someday.

senses.definition: The part of your body that holds food after you swallow it and mixes it with juices.
senses.example: Food moves from the stomach into the small intestine.

senses.definition: Strong and able to stand up to weight, use, or bumps.
senses.example: We packed the books in a sturdy box.

senses.definition: A word part added at the end of a word or word part. It can change the meaning or how a word works in a sentence.
senses.example: Adding the suffix -less to care makes careless.

senses.definition: The right to vote in an election.
senses.example: Supporters of women’s suffrage worked for women to be able to vote.

senses.definition: To move through water by moving your body, legs, fins, or arms.
senses.example: The ducks swam across the pond in a line.

senses.definition: One beat or part of a spoken word, usually built around a vowel sound.
senses.example: Clap once for each syllable in butterfly: but-ter-fly.
